section_summary: This section concerns the identification, custody, examination, and proposed disposition of former Japanese diplomatic and consular archives and property after World War II. It includes a detailed list of Belgian employees and associates of the Japanese Embassy in Brussels; correspondence about archives in Brazil, Canada, China, Chile, Argentina, and New Zealand; policy papers on Allied authority over Japanese property; and an extensive four-power report on the Japanese Legation archives in Mexico. The Mexican report describes consular records, petroleum shipments, migration plans, coded telegrams, propaganda, intelligence material, and Japanese relations with Germany, China, Russia, Mexico, and the United States.

subfiles.title: List of Persons Believed to Be Japanese Embassy Employees
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Brussels
subfiles.about: Lists persons believed to have worked for, lived with, or been closely related to employees of the former Japanese Embassy in Brussels.
subfiles.summary: The list supplies names, birth details, addresses, nationalities, occupations, and family relationships for Belgian and former Russian personnel connected with the embassy. It covers translators, chauffeurs, servants, secretaries, porters, a maître d'hôtel, and members of their households.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Lists of Pro- and Anti-Japanese Persons and Others to the Navy Department
subfiles.from: Saxton E. Bradford, Department of State
subfiles.to: Rear Admiral J. L. McCrea, Navy Department
subfiles.about: Transmits three translated lists recovered from the former Japanese Embassy in Brussels.
subfiles.summary: Bradford sends the Navy lists of pro-, anti- and neutral persons, films and suspected Japanese Embassy employees, French originals found in Brussels embassy archives and translated by State.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Lists of Pro- and Anti-Japanese Persons and Others to the FBI
subfiles.from: Saxton E. Bradford, Department of State
subfiles.to: Ralph Roach, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: Sends the FBI copies of three lists taken from the former Japanese Embassy archives in Brussels.
subfiles.summary: Bradford sends the FBI the same lists of politically aligned persons, films and suspected embassy employees from the Brussels archives.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Lists of Pro- and Anti-Japanese Persons and Others to Military Intelligence
subfiles.from: Saxton E. Bradford, Department of State
subfiles.to: Major Winn Zeller, Military Intelligence Service
subfiles.about: Forwards translated Brussels embassy lists to the War Department's Military Intelligence Service.
subfiles.summary: Memorandum encloses lists of pro-, anti- and neutral persons, films and suspected employees from the former Japanese Embassy in Brussels for Military Intelligence.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Lists of Former Japanese Property at Bauru
subfiles.from: Cecil M. P. Cross, American Consul General, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Transmits an inventory of twenty-three cases of material formerly held by the Japanese Consulate at Bauru.
subfiles.summary: Cross forwards two copies of the inventory of cases holding the former Japanese consulate's archives and property at Bauru, with a copy to Rio.

subfiles.title: Inventory of Twenty-Three Cases from the Japanese Consulate at Bauru
subfiles.from: American Consulate General, São Paulo
subfiles.about: Itemizes books, registration records, office equipment, and silverware found in twenty-three cases from the former Japanese Consulate at Bauru.
subfiles.summary: The inventory lists books, immigrant and family registration cards, vital-record files, Japanese laws, stationery, a typewriter, and household objects. It separately enumerates an 1847 Rogers Brothers silver service and other silver or brass pieces.

subfiles.title: Availability of Japanese Diplomatic and Consular Archives in Canada
subfiles.from: Ray Atherton, American Embassy, Ottawa
subfiles.about: Reports that Japanese archives assembled in Ottawa are ready for examination and asks how to answer Canada's invitation to participate.
subfiles.summary: Atherton, noting Canada will not start examination until the US decides to participate, requests prompt instructions on Japanese archives, including Vancouver material.

subfiles.title: Canadian Invitation to Examine Japanese Archives Jointly
subfiles.from: H. H. Wrong, Department of External Affairs
subfiles.to: Ray Atherton, United States Ambassador to Canada
subfiles.about: Invites appropriate United States officials to join Canada in examining Japanese legation and consular archives.
subfiles.summary: Wrong says the records are now in Ottawa and Canada will defer its examination pending the US decision.

subfiles.title: Request for War Department Participation in the Canadian Archive Examination
subfiles.from: Saxton E. Bradford, Department of State
subfiles.to: Lieutenant Colonel H. St. Clair, Captured Documents Center
subfiles.about: Asks the War Department to appoint a representative for a joint examination of Japanese archives in Ottawa.
subfiles.summary: Bradford reports the US accepted Canada's invitation and will send a State representative; asks the War Department for a second representative.

subfiles.title: Acceptance of Canada's Invitation to Examine Japanese Archives
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Authorizes the embassy to tell Canada that the United States accepts the invitation to participate in a joint archive examination.
subfiles.summary: Department will send a representative to examine Canada's Japanese archives and has asked the War Department to do likewise.

subfiles.title: Instructions Concerning a SCAP-Sponsored Request to China
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Explains that any approach to China concerning Japanese records will be made through the political adviser in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: War Department is informing SCAP in response to the embassy; Nanking is advised so it can act if a SCAP-sponsored request develops.

subfiles.title: Instructions for Examination of Japanese Archives in New Zealand
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Approves a request to New Zealand for early access to Japanese archives and suggests alternatives if language limitations impede examination.
subfiles.summary: Department authorizes examination of Japanese archives in New Zealand and suggests sending selected material or photostats to the Department if the committee cannot use it.

subfiles.title: Proposed Examination of Japanese Archives in Wellington
subfiles.from: Avra M. Warren, American Legation, Wellington
subfiles.about: Reports the transfer of Japanese archives from Swiss custody and proposes a joint American examination committee.
subfiles.summary: Wellington: New Zealand will postpone examination for lack of personnel but seems willing to allow the Legation access; Warren proposes a committee of attachés and Marshall Green.

subfiles.title: Chinese Willingness to Assist with Former Japanese Consular Archives
subfiles.from: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Reports China's response to inquiries about Japanese consular and diplomatic records still located there.
subfiles.summary: China is prepared to assist SCAP or Japanese agencies needing to consult former consular files, answering the Department's attempt to learn whether records may go to Japan or be inspected in China.

subfiles.title: Chinese Affairs Recommendation on Japanese Consular Records
subfiles.from: E. F. Drumright, Division of Chinese Affairs
subfiles.to: R. E. Hibbard, Special Projects Division
subfiles.about: Recommends asking the American Embassy at Nanking to determine whether China will permit specified Japanese consular court records to be removed.
subfiles.summary: Drumright considers the records of little use for ordinary American services or litigation and regards Chinese consent to removal as the central question. An appended draft enumerates eleven categories, including judgments, notarial deeds, criminal records, property registers, and census materials.

subfiles.title: Special Projects Division Objections to an Immediate Approach to China
subfiles.from: R. E. Hibbard, Special Projects Division
subfiles.to: E. F. Drumright, Division of Chinese Affairs
subfiles.about: Argues for gathering more information and coordinating Department views before formally asking China to release Japanese archives.
subfiles.summary: Hibbard says the Japanese request may constitute an exception to SCAP's worldwide archive directive and could affect precedents elsewhere. He also notes that the records may document transfers of American property during the occupation and therefore favors a preliminary inquiry to Shanghai before approaching the Chinese government.

subfiles.title: Draft Inquiry to Shanghai on Japanese Consular Records
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Solicits views on retaining Japanese consular court and civil-registration records in China for American legal and consular needs.
subfiles.summary: Unsent draft to Shanghai lists eleven categories of records requested by the Japanese Central Liaison Office and asks whether they should stay in China for American interests.

subfiles.title: War Department Request Concerning Records of Japanese Consulates in China
subfiles.from: C. V. Allan, Military Intelligence Service
subfiles.to: Albert E. Clattenburg, Department of State
subfiles.about: Requests State Department action to obtain Chinese consent for release of former Japanese consular and diplomatic records.
subfiles.summary: Military Intelligence Service forwards the Japanese request and SCAP correspondence, suggesting negotiation outcomes be reported to SCAP through the political adviser.

subfiles.title: SCAP Recommendation on Japanese Consular Records in China
subfiles.from: B. M. Fitch, General Headquarters, SCAP
subfiles.about: Recommends securing Chinese governmental consent for the return of Japanese consular court records and possibly all Japanese consular documents.
subfiles.summary: SCAP notes American forces in China may gain intelligence from the Japanese consular records but collection or return needs governmental agreement with China.

subfiles.title: Request for Permission to Bring Consular Court Documents from China
subfiles.from: S. Iguchi, Japanese Central Liaison Office
subfiles.about: Requests permission to transfer eleven classes of former Japanese consular court and civil-registration records from China to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The request covers judgments, mediation and arbitration files, notarial records, criminal histories, pending proceedings, fines, property and commercial registers, and census documents. It argues that the records are needed to resume legal proceedings involving repatriates, determine property rights, conduct lawsuits, and reconstruct civil-registration entries lost in transit or air raids.

subfiles.title: Chinese Affairs Objections to the Shanghai Draft Telegram
subfiles.from: E. F. Drumright, Division of Chinese Affairs
subfiles.to: R. E. Hibbard, Special Projects Division
subfiles.about: Declines to approve the proposed Shanghai inquiry and recommends addressing the Embassy at Nanking instead.
subfiles.summary: Drumright argues the Shanghai inquiry should reflect the Japanese request and the records' general value; he expects China to keep them for property and reparations disputes but perhaps allow local inspection.

subfiles.title: Inquiry to Nanking on Removal or Inspection of Japanese Records
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Directs the embassy to ascertain China's attitude toward removing Japanese records or allowing them to be assembled and copied in China.
subfiles.summary: The telegram enumerates the eleven requested classes of judicial, property, commercial, and census records. It also asks for the embassy's assessment of their usefulness to the United States in consular services or litigation involving American interests.

subfiles.title: Archives of the Ex-Japanese Embassy and Consulate in Argentina, Despatch No. 212
subfiles.from: John M. Cabot, American Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: Reports the shipment of the most important Japanese diplomatic and consular archives from Argentina in four steamer pouches.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 212: Cabot says the contents of three trunks go with Despatch 213 in four boxes assigned to steamer pouch numbers.

subfiles.title: Withdrawal Notice for Restricted Item
subfiles.from: National Archives / General Services Administration
subfiles.about: Records the removal of a June 1946 item from the file because access was restricted.
subfiles.summary: Withdrawal notice for a restricted item containing security-classified information.

subfiles.title: Status of Plans to Send Japanese Archives from Chile to Washington
subfiles.from: Claude G. Bowers, American Embassy, Santiago
subfiles.about: Explains that the arrival of the Soviet ambassador has delayed an agreed plan to send Japanese archives from Chile to Washington.
subfiles.summary: Santiago: Allied representatives agreed to ship Japanese archives by US Navy aircraft; the Soviet ambassador must be offered inspection and asked whether he accepts the shipment plan.

subfiles.title: Archives of the Ex-Japanese Embassy and Consulate in Argentina, Duplicate Despatch No. 212
subfiles.from: John M. Cabot, American Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: Duplicate copy reporting the shipment of four boxes containing major portions of the Japanese archives in Argentina.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate Despatch 212 recording the four steamer pouches used to forward the contents of three archival trunks.

subfiles.title: Archives of the Ex-Japanese Embassy and Consulate in Argentina, Despatch No. 213
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: Forwards four boxes of former Japanese Embassy and consular archives and identifies the attached box inventories.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 213: the material comes from three trunks; four enclosures list the contents of boxes each assigned to a separate steamer pouch.

subfiles.title: Contents of Argentine Archive Box No. 1
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: Lists folders and record books packed in the first archival box.
subfiles.summary: Box 1 holds folders 1-14 from Trunk I, two record books from Trunk III and two Trunk I notebooks, in steamer pouch 4754.

subfiles.title: Contents of Argentine Archive Box No. 2
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: Lists the contents of the second box of Japanese records shipped from Argentina.
subfiles.summary: Box 2 holds thirteen black-bound record books and folders 15-28 from Trunk I, shipped in steamer pouch 5094.

subfiles.title: Contents of Argentine Archive Box No. 3
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: Lists folders and bound records placed in the third archive box.
subfiles.summary: Box 3 holds folders 29-42 from Trunk II, two record books and folders C-1 and C-2 from Trunk III, in steamer pouch 5255.

subfiles.title: Contents of Argentine Archive Box No. 4
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.about: Identifies the final group of folders shipped in Box No. 4.
subfiles.summary: The box contains folders C-3 through C-20 from Trunk III. It was sent in steamer pouch No. 6758.

subfiles.title: DC/R Routing Slip
subfiles.from: Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.about: Blank or nearly blank internal routing sheet associated with the Argentine archive shipment.
subfiles.summary: Routing slip with only the heading and fields; no legible instructions.

subfiles.title: Japanese Property in Brazil
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Rio de Janeiro
subfiles.about: Reports Brazilian discussion of Japanese government property and asks how former embassy funds and assets should ultimately be disposed of.
subfiles.summary: Embassy talks with Brazilian officials on custody of Japanese archives and property, funds in Bank of Brazil accounts, São Paulo property and Swedish Legation assets; requests Department policy on disposal.

subfiles.title: Memorandum to Brazil on Custody of Japanese Archives and Property
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Rio de Janeiro
subfiles.about: Seeks Brazil's views on procedures for securing Japanese archives and property on behalf of the four Allied powers.
subfiles.summary: Memorandum to Brazil: the US acts for itself, Britain, the USSR and China to prevent destruction of Japanese material, expects Sweden to relinquish assets, and asks how custody should be arranged.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Proposed Revision to the MacArthur Directive
subfiles.from: J. W. Amshey
subfiles.to: Albert E. Clattenburg, Special Projects Division
subfiles.about: Forwards a SWNCC paper proposing revision of the directive governing Japanese diplomatic property and archives.
subfiles.summary: Amshey notes Far Eastern Affairs thinks the four powers' representatives, not a revised MacArthur directive, should decide disposition; asks Clattenburg for the next step.

subfiles.title: SWNCC Routing Note
subfiles.from: W. L. Wasley
subfiles.about: Returns a State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee paper following an earlier conversation.
subfiles.summary: SWNCC routing sheet with a handwritten forwarding note; no policy discussion.

subfiles.title: Memorandum Recommending SWNCC Consideration of an Amendment
subfiles.from: John H. Hilldring, State Department member of SWNCC
subfiles.about: Recommends referral of a State-approved amendment to the October 1945 directive on Japanese diplomatic property and archives.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring asks SWNCC to consider a paper proposing an amendment on disposition of property and archives of former Japanese diplomatic missions.

subfiles.title: Custody of Japanese Archives and Diplomatic Property
subfiles.from: Department of State / State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee
subfiles.about: Proposes amendments clarifying Allied authority over Japanese diplomatic property while preserving true archives intact.
subfiles.summary: The paper explains practical problems created by a literal requirement for physical custody, including storage costs, depreciating goods, and politically dangerous propaganda material. It proposes allowing the four powers to liquidate movable official and personal property when appropriate while holding proceeds for ultimate reparations settlement. Official documents, consular registers, and relevant correspondence would remain intact, while propaganda, libraries, stamps, seals, flags, and insignia could be destroyed by agreement.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Memorandum Recommending SWNCC Consideration
subfiles.from: John H. Hilldring, State Department member of SWNCC
subfiles.about: Duplicate or alternate copy recommending committee consideration of the proposed amendment on Japanese diplomatic property.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate memorandum recommending a State-approved paper be referred to SWNCC, with clearance notations.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Policy Paper on Custody of Japanese Archives and Diplomatic Property
subfiles.from: Department of State / State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee
subfiles.about: Duplicate text of the proposal to revise Allied policy for Japanese diplomatic archives and movable property.
subfiles.summary: This copy again describes the costs and difficulties of retaining all property physically intact and the divergent interpretations adopted by the four Allied powers. It authorizes liquidation of suitable movable property while preserving proceeds for reparations and keeping genuine archives intact. Propaganda and similar non-archival material could be destroyed, and rapidly depreciating personal effects could be sold to preserve their value.

subfiles.title: Examination of Archives and Miscellaneous Papers Found in the Japanese Legation, Mexico City
subfiles.from: Walter J. Linthicum, American Embassy, Mexico City
subfiles.about: Transmits the report of the four-power commission that examined the former Japanese Legation archives in Mexico City.
subfiles.summary: Linthicum reports that representatives of China, the Soviet Union, Great Britain, and the United States examined the material between April 25 and June 25, 1946. Chinese and Soviet members translated Japanese documents, and the archives were then boxed and stored in the American Embassy basement pending instructions.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on the Examination of the Japanese Legation Archives in Mexico City
subfiles.from: Four-power archive examining commission, Mexico City
subfiles.to: American Embassy, Mexico City / Department of State
subfiles.about: Reports the contents and significance of archival volumes and miscellaneous papers recovered from the former Japanese Legation in Mexico.
subfiles.summary: The commission describes consular citizenship, vital-statistics, passport, immigration, demographic, financial, and correspondence files, together with records of major Mexican petroleum shipments to Japan and offers of minerals. Historical telegram books cover Japanese-American relations, the 1924 U.S. immigration law, plans to settle thousands of Japanese farmers in Mexico, Russo-Japanese relations, arms sales to Mexico, oil interests, radio communications, and diplomatic reporting. Loose papers include Japanese alien-control regulations, German requests for passage aboard Japanese ships, pro-Japanese correspondence, code groups, and intelligence pamphlets on oil, news agencies, China, Manchuria, and world intelligence services. The report continues beyond page 503.
